Generated from the exact pinned XML identifiers and reviewed `mapping.json`; do not edit this file.

The type plan locates all retained public types, including entirely pending types. Candidate paths describe work allocation and do not assert that a Rust type exists or that it is equivalent. Every pending member remains listed in [api-members.json](api-members.json). A partial mapping records only the behavior described with its target, tests and deviation; it does not close the whole native contract.

### `Microsoft.UI.Text.FindOptions`

The native implementation is external to the pinned repository. Review this exact enum/format/service contract and its consumers before claiming equivalent behavior.

#### `F:Microsoft.UI.Text.FindOptions.Case`

State: **partial**. Native numeric flags and FerroUI markup metadata are declared by the Rust type. This record does not count declaration of an unsupported flag as functional implementation of that mode.

State: **partial**. Inherited CultureInfo Language and CharacterFormat language patches use pinned XML-language validation, platform preferred language/en-US default, and existing culture-aware shaping/font fallback. ### `Microsoft.UI.Text.ITextParagraphFormat`

Audit native formatting units, mixed values, font/brush representation, tabs, lists, language resolution and formatting flags. Inherited language and supported RTF locale IDs have explicit mappings; Rust patches cover only reviewed fields.

#### `M:Microsoft.UI.Text.ITextParagraphFormat.AddTab(System.Single,Microsoft.UI.Text.TabAlignment,Microsoft.UI.Text.TabLeader)`

State: **partial**. Immutable sorted tab configurations support native-valued alignment/leaders, points-to-layout conversion, replacement at an existing position, zero-based lookup, nonmutating validation, removal and clearing. Explicit stops are limited to 63; equal default stops remain when explicit tabs are cleared. Rich paragraph snapshots, format queries, splits and undo preserve the value. Native TOM ABI and mixed-property facade semantics remain separate.

### `Microsoft.UI.Text.ITextRange`

Audit the external TOM contract member by member. The Rust facade uses typed errors, UTF-16 text ranges and shared editor services; remaining option behavior, ABI and native units are not inferred from similarly named methods. Eight native-valued units including shaped Cluster, explicit Rust Read/Write adapters, paragraph tabs and structured Unicode case conversion have individual mappings; locale/engine conformance and unmapped members remain pending.

#### `M:Microsoft.UI.Text.ITextRange.CanPaste(System.Int32)`

State: **partial**. The TOM clipboard family uses injected FerroUI IClipboard and LocalBoxFuture services. BestAvailable chooses exact in-process content, then supported RTF aliases, then Unicode text; explicit PlainText/Rtf never fall back outside the requested representation. CanPaste checks fallible advertised formats without decoding payloads, ending composition or modifying history. Document CanCopy is permission, independent of selection length and edit read-only state; the current model has no copy-protection policy. Copy captures immutable visible content. Nonempty Cut ends an original preview before capturing committed content, then deletes only after a successful write and current-target validation; a failed write does not restart that preview. Paste validates/parses/limits before canceling an original preview and recaptures committed live endpoints. Empty or rejected content cannot delete the target. Plain text inherits insertion formatting; rich fragments retain supported structure; directed editor selection is rebased and the edit forms one undo group. Document mutation identity, shared range/format generation and a disposable editor-change subscription reject stale asynchronous edits, including away-and-back changes and held batches. Retrieved transfers dispose on success, error or future cancellation and before final validation; outgoing transfers belong to the clipboard. These asynchronous named-format APIs are an intentional Rust translation, not synchronous native ABI or arbitrary numeric-format support. Native copy/per-range protection, OLE cloning, unsupported formats/RTF grammar, terminal EOP and external WinUI behavior remain pending. Control routed clipboard events/casing policy is separate from this independent TOM range service. Test definitions and completed execution evidence are recorded separately.

#### `M:Microsoft.UI.Text.ITextRange.Cut`

State: **partial**. The TOM clipboard family uses injected FerroUI IClipboard and LocalBoxFuture services. BestAvailable chooses exact in-process content, then supported RTF aliases, then Unicode text; explicit PlainText/Rtf never fall back outside the requested representation. CanPaste checks fallible advertised formats without decoding payloads, ending composition or modifying history. Document CanCopy is permission, independent of selection length and edit read-only state; the current model has no copy-protection policy. Copy captures immutable visible content. Nonempty Cut ends an original preview before capturing committed content, then deletes only after a successful write and current-target validation; a failed write does not restart that preview. Paste validates/parses/limits before canceling an original preview and recaptures committed live endpoints. Empty or rejected content cannot delete the target. Plain text inherits insertion formatting; rich fragments retain supported structure; directed editor selection is rebased and the edit forms one undo group. Document mutation identity, shared range/format generation and a disposable editor-change subscription reject stale asynchronous edits, including away-and-back changes and held batches. Retrieved transfers dispose on success, error or future cancellation and before final validation; outgoing transfers belong to the clipboard. These asynchronous named-format APIs are an intentional Rust translation, not synchronous native ABI or arbitrary numeric-format support. Native copy/per-range protection, OLE cloning, unsupported formats/RTF grammar, terminal EOP and external WinUI behavior remain pending. Control routed clipboard events/casing policy is separate from this independent TOM range service. Test definitions and completed execution evidence are recorded separately.

#### `M:Microsoft.UI.Text.ITextRange.Delete(Microsoft.UI.Text.TextRangeUnit,System.Int32)`

State: **partial**. Delete removes a nonempty range first and counts it once, then resolves remaining signed logical units against the changed document. Count zero removes only the selected span; extreme counts do not overflow. Supported paragraph joins retain the surviving following paragraph format, preserve local/inherited character provenance, rebase independent selection and collapse the edited range in one undo unit. The selection facade recaptures after layout callbacks. Proven external model changes during layout or publication survive rejection without stale history/selection rollback; ordinary errors still roll back. The Rust result is a nonnegative usize removed-unit count. Only the eight mapped units and normalized model positions are supported; native structural markers, additional units and native engine conformance remain pending.

#### `M:Microsoft.UI.Text.ITextRange.EndOf(Microsoft.UI.Text.TextRangeUnit,System.Boolean)`

State: **partial**. end_of operates on live scalar-safe UTF-16 ranges. Start/end use signed displacements, indices are one-based or end-relative, and movement counts a nonempty collapse as its first unit. The eight implemented constants retain native numeric values. Character traverses Unicode scalars, Word includes following ASCII blanks, Sentence follows native punctuation rules, Paragraph handles native separators, HardParagraph distinguishes structural paragraphs from soft breaks, and Line uses a weak complete untrimmed view with headless Paragraph fallback. The model has one Story and excludes the synthetic terminal CR. Remaining native units, arbitrary stories and ABI remain pending. Shaped Cluster uses the same movement/index operations and requires complete validated live layout.

#### `M:Microsoft.UI.Text.ITextRange.GetIndex(Microsoft.UI.Text.TextRangeUnit)`

State: **partial**. get_index operates on live scalar-safe UTF-16 ranges. Start/end use signed displacements, indices are one-based or end-relative, and movement counts a nonempty collapse as its first unit. The eight implemented constants retain native numeric values. Character traverses Unicode scalars, Word includes following ASCII blanks, Sentence follows native punctuation rules, Paragraph handles native separators, HardParagraph distinguishes structural paragraphs from soft breaks, and Line uses a weak complete untrimmed view with headless Paragraph fallback. The model has one Story and excludes the synthetic terminal CR. Remaining native units, arbitrary stories and ABI remain pending. Shaped Cluster uses the same movement/index operations and requires complete validated live layout.

#### `M:Microsoft.UI.Text.ITextRange.MoveStart(Microsoft.UI.Text.TextRangeUnit,System.Int32)`

State: **partial**. move_start operates on live scalar-safe UTF-16 ranges. Start/end use signed displacements, indices are one-based or end-relative, and movement counts a nonempty collapse as its first unit. The eight implemented constants retain native numeric values. Character traverses Unicode scalars, Word includes following ASCII blanks, Sentence follows native punctuation rules, Paragraph handles native separators, HardParagraph distinguishes structural paragraphs from soft breaks, and Line uses a weak complete untrimmed view with headless Paragraph fallback. The model has one Story and excludes the synthetic terminal CR. Remaining native units, arbitrary stories and ABI remain pending. Shaped Cluster uses the same movement/index operations and requires complete validated live layout.

#### `M:Microsoft.UI.Text.ITextRange.Paste(System.Int32)`

State: **partial**. The TOM clipboard family uses injected FerroUI IClipboard and LocalBoxFuture services. BestAvailable chooses exact in-process content, then supported RTF aliases, then Unicode text; explicit PlainText/Rtf never fall back outside the requested representation. CanPaste checks fallible advertised formats without decoding payloads, ending composition or modifying history. Document CanCopy is permission, independent of selection length and edit read-only state; the current model has no copy-protection policy. Copy captures immutable visible content. Nonempty Cut ends an original preview before capturing committed content, then deletes only after a successful write and current-target validation; a failed write does not restart that preview. Paste validates/parses/limits before canceling an original preview and recaptures committed live endpoints. Empty or rejected content cannot delete the target. Plain text inherits insertion formatting; rich fragments retain supported structure; directed editor selection is rebased and the edit forms one undo group. Document mutation identity, shared range/format generation and a disposable editor-change subscription reject stale asynchronous edits, including away-and-back changes and held batches. Retrieved transfers dispose on success, error or future cancellation and before final validation; outgoing transfers belong to the clipboard. These asynchronous named-format APIs are an intentional Rust translation, not synchronous native ABI or arbitrary numeric-format support. Native copy/per-range protection, OLE cloning, unsupported formats/RTF grammar, terminal EOP and external WinUI behavior remain pending. Control routed clipboard events/casing policy is separate from this independent TOM range service. Test definitions and completed execution evidence are recorded separately.

#### `M:Microsoft.UI.Text.ITextRange.SetText(Microsoft.UI.Text.TextSetOptions,System.String)`

State: **partial**. Typed get_text/set_text_with_options implement the mapped plain/RTF projections, CR/CRLF/LF and terminal-paragraph handling, scalar-safe length policy, atomic parse/option validation and supported Unlink insertion. The native UseLfAndUseCrLf assertions are adapted directly. Object-text, numbering, hidden-text filtering/unhiding, UnicodeBidi insertion mode and ApplyRtfDocumentDefaults return explicit UnsupportedOptions; unknown/contradictory flags fail before editing. The model retains normalized UTF-16 text coordinates and the codec remains a bounded RTF subset. Portable byte decoding supports 874, 932, 936, 949, 950, 1250..1258, 10000, 10007 and 65001 through pinned encoding_rs tables. Raw/escaped multibyte tokens share one incremental UTF-16 decoder; malformed input and incomplete sequences at syntax boundaries fail without replacement. Font-scoped fcharset/cpg, default-font/plain resets, font names and field destinations share that codec. Symbol/OEM/Johab and unspecified pages remain explicit errors. Export retains the canonical Unicode-escaped writer; byte-for-byte native code-page roundtrip and full RTF content are not claimed. Paragraph/character stylesheet references now resolve forward based-on chains, additive formatting and subsequent direct overrides through the shared property decoder, with cycle/kind/reference/depth checks and an independent expansion work budget. Ignored style names/keycodes/metadata never become story text. Resolved appearance is retained; live named-style identity, next-style policies and section/table styles are not implemented. Hyperlink field results spanning paragraphs become separate paragraph-owned links with identical URI/target and retained metrics/formatting; empty paragraphs create no invisible links. Cumulative materialized URI/target bytes are checked against max_bytes before cloning. Imports finish parsing before model/history/preview mutation. Native field identity and full content/format conformance remain pending.

#### `M:Microsoft.UI.Text.ITextRange.SetTextViaStream(Microsoft.UI.Text.TextSetOptions,Windows.Storage.Streams.IRandomAccessStream)`

State: **partial**. The native random-access stream ABI is translated to FerroUI-style Rust Read/Write. TextStreamOptions explicitly selects plain UTF-8/UTF-16LE/UTF-16BE, BOM and byte bounds; RTF uses raw codec bytes. Input validation finishes before mutation, output encoding before writing, and caller ownership/current position are preserved. Unsupported flags/content fail explicitly; native engine encoding defaults and WinRT ABI are not inferred. Portable byte decoding supports 874, 932, 936, 949, 950, 1250..1258, 10000, 10007 and 65001 through pinned encoding_rs tables. Raw/escaped multibyte tokens share one incremental UTF-16 decoder; malformed input and incomplete sequences at syntax boundaries fail without replacement. Font-scoped fcharset/cpg, default-font/plain resets, font names and field destinations share that codec. Symbol/OEM/Johab and unspecified pages remain explicit errors. Export retains the canonical Unicode-escaped writer; byte-for-byte native code-page roundtrip and full RTF content are not claimed. Paragraph/character stylesheet references now resolve forward based-on chains, additive formatting and subsequent direct overrides through the shared property decoder, with cycle/kind/reference/depth checks and an independent expansion work budget. Ignored style names/keycodes/metadata never become story text. Resolved appearance is retained; live named-style identity, next-style policies and section/table styles are not implemented. Hyperlink field results spanning paragraphs become separate paragraph-owned links with identical URI/target and retained metrics/formatting; empty paragraphs create no invisible links. Cumulative materialized URI/target bytes are checked against max_bytes before cloning. Imports finish parsing before model/history/preview mutation. Native field identity and full content/format conformance remain pending.

#### `M:Microsoft.UI.Text.ITextRange.StartOf(Microsoft.UI.Text.TextRangeUnit,System.Boolean)`

State: **partial**. start_of operates on live scalar-safe UTF-16 ranges. Start/end use signed displacements, indices are one-based or end-relative, and movement counts a nonempty collapse as its first unit. The eight implemented constants retain native numeric values. Character traverses Unicode scalars, Word includes following ASCII blanks, Sentence follows native punctuation rules, Paragraph handles native separators, HardParagraph distinguishes structural paragraphs from soft breaks, and Line uses a weak complete untrimmed view with headless Paragraph fallback. The model has one Story and excludes the synthetic terminal CR. Remaining native units, arbitrary stories and ABI remain pending. Shaped Cluster uses the same movement/index operations and requires complete validated live layout.

#### `P:Microsoft.UI.Text.ITextRange.Character`

State: **partial**. Character reads the exact UTF-16 code unit at the range start, including a leading surrogate, and returns zero at the model end. The u16 setter rejects isolated surrogate input and replacement of half an existing pair; Rust scalar getter/setter extensions handle complete supplementary characters safely. Replacement retains assigned run/container/paragraph formatting and inheritance, the range start, independent directed selection, scalar-safe length policy and one undo unit. Preflight validation/no-op calls preserve composition and redo; changed calls cancel preview then recapture committed content, which can itself be unchanged. Detected external writes retain their model while stale history/composition is discarded. Native synthetic terminal CR and transient malformed UTF-16 are not model characters; native engine conformance remains pending.

#### `P:Microsoft.UI.Text.ITextRange.Gravity`

State: **partial**. Independent ranges retain native-valued formatting affinity, including measured Outward-to-UI readback and duplicate reset-to-UI. Collapsed format queries and plain SetText/paste use the same previous/following-run resolution; explicit patches override the resolved source, and paragraph formatting stays with the current paragraph. Native 45 affinity, ten retention and 24 invalid fixtures are literal tests. Range generations preserve newer callback ownership and invalidate pending clipboard work; grouped edits restore the exact independent typing snapshot. Native physical endpoint rebasing differs from current TextPointer tracking and is not changed here. The model excludes a synthetic terminal EOP, so forward story-end affinity samples final paragraph defaults; signed native clamping is adapted to scalar-safe usize/Result validation. The actual selection's inherited Gravity behavior and the external WinUI engine remain unmeasured. Range metadata is not document history; successful undo and failed outer text groups retain accepted explicit mode changes as a stated FerroUI policy.

### `Microsoft.UI.Text.ITextSelection`

Audit the external TOM contract member by member. The Rust facade uses typed errors, UTF-16 text ranges and shared editor services; remaining option behavior, ABI and native units are not inferred from similarly named methods. Eight native-valued units including shaped Cluster, explicit Rust Read/Write adapters, paragraph tabs and structured Unicode case conversion have individual mappings; locale/engine conformance and unmapped members remain pending.

#### `M:Microsoft.UI.Text.ITextSelection.EndKey(Microsoft.UI.Text.TextRangeUnit,System.Boolean)`

State: **partial**. Line/Story Home/End now uses the normalized first/last selected line when collapsing and the directed active endpoint when extending. Extended Line End includes a real hard paragraph mark and retains source-line end affinity across repeated calls; a collapsed End excludes that mark. These endpoint choices are derived from the recorded system MSFTEDIT run, not assumed from conflicting documentation wording. The result is accepted signed UTF-16 displacement after cancellable/reentrant selection handlers. Line uses complete untrimmed shaping and linked overflow, with paragraph fallback when headless. Read-only navigation preserves active composition and redo; layout/selection/publication model-write fences retain external state and reject stale acknowledgement. An independent navigation generation protects newer callback-owned view/affinity decisions even at identical selection offsets. The model excludes native synthetic terminal EOP; soft-break/wrap extension affinity, general Gravity and the external WinUI engine remain separate conformance boundaries.

State: **partial**. Line/Story Home/End now uses the normalized first/last selected line when collapsing and the directed active endpoint when extending. Extended Line End includes a real hard paragraph mark and retains source-line end affinity across repeated calls; a collapsed End excludes that mark. State: **partial**. Rust MoveUp/MoveDown accept Line and Paragraph. Line uses complete untrimmed shaped display lines, caret hit testing and linked-overflow geometry; Paragraph uses logical boundaries without a view. Collapsed movement retains the desired physical column across short lines. Extension projects from each actual reached caret and clamps through intervening short/empty lines, while preserving an earlier collapsed desired column for later collapsed movement. Signed counts widen and saturate; work is bounded by actual crossed lines. A nonempty collapse starts at the directional edge and applies the full distance; collapse alone counts once. Accepted units account for cancellation, redirection and real story-edge units. Mutation, selection, view and navigation generations protect callback-owned state; same-view reassociation preserves affinity. The 290-command native record adds eight mixed-mode observations to the unchanged previous 282. Literal mixed-mode, geometry-cost and ownership fixtures executed in the 70-test focused selection gate published at f10fb838. Additional edge projection runs only after accepted edge redirection. Screen/Window, synthetic terminal EOP, general Gravity and external WinUI engine equivalence remain pending. Shared formatter marker geometry is independently tested; this is not pixel parity.

#### `M:Microsoft.UI.Text.ITextSelection.MoveLeft(Microsoft.UI.Text.TextRangeUnit,System.Int32,System.Boolean)`

State: **partial**. Rust MoveLeft/MoveRight accept Character and Word without a view. Keyboard Character uses FerroUI GraphemeEnumerator boundaries independently of scalar range Character. Word uses the reviewed logical boundaries. Signed counts reverse, zero validates units, and widened extreme counts saturate without request-sized iteration. Nonextended Character collapses to its directional exact edge and consumes one unit; Word aligns the edge to its directional boundary and consumes one. Extension retains the anchor. The logical source-offset policy matches observed default and RTL-reading fixtures, without claiming visual bidi or general Gravity parity. Literal regressions replay 294 of 300 native rows, including 78 new aligned-word/grapheme-interior observations; six synthetic terminal-EOP rows remain outside normalized Rust coordinates. Publication preserves callback cancellation/redirection, external edits and nested navigation, reports accepted counts and clears old vertical affinity. The completed 70-test focused selection gate at f10fb838 executes these fixtures. Synthetic terminal EOP and external WinUI engine parity remain pending.

#### `M:Microsoft.UI.Text.ITextSelection.TypeText(System.String)`

State: **partial**. Typing uses the shared editor and its actual Overtype mode. Each accepted input scalar consumes one target grapheme; a selected range is consumed by the first scalar. Typed CR and LF insert separate paragraph breaks without consuming target text, so typed CRLF differs from bulk newline normalization. #### `M:Microsoft.UI.Text.RichEditTextDocument.CanCopy`

State: **partial**. The TOM clipboard family uses injected FerroUI IClipboard and LocalBoxFuture services. BestAvailable chooses exact in-process content, then supported RTF aliases, then Unicode text; explicit PlainText/Rtf never fall back outside the requested representation. CanPaste checks fallible advertised formats without decoding payloads, ending composition or modifying history. Document CanCopy is permission, independent of selection length and edit read-only state; the current model has no copy-protection policy. Copy captures immutable visible content. Nonempty Cut ends an original preview before capturing committed content, then deletes only after a successful write and current-target validation; a failed write does not restart that preview. Paste validates/parses/limits before canceling an original preview and recaptures committed live endpoints. Empty or rejected content cannot delete the target. Plain text inherits insertion formatting; rich fragments retain supported structure; directed editor selection is rebased and the edit forms one undo group. Document mutation identity, shared range/format generation and a disposable editor-change subscription reject stale asynchronous edits, including away-and-back changes and held batches. Retrieved transfers dispose on success, error or future cancellation and before final validation; outgoing transfers belong to the clipboard. These asynchronous named-format APIs are an intentional Rust translation, not synchronous native ABI or arbitrary numeric-format support. Native copy/per-range protection, OLE cloning, unsupported formats/RTF grammar, terminal EOP and external WinUI behavior remain pending. Control routed clipboard events/casing policy is separate from this independent TOM range service. Test definitions and completed execution evidence are recorded separately.

#### `M:Microsoft.UI.Text.RichEditTextDocument.LoadFromStream(Microsoft.UI.Text.TextSetOptions,Windows.Storage.Streams.IRandomAccessStream)`

State: **partial**. The native random-access stream ABI is translated to FerroUI-style Rust Read/Write. TextStreamOptions explicitly selects plain UTF-8/UTF-16LE/UTF-16BE, BOM and byte bounds; RTF uses raw codec bytes. Input validation finishes before mutation, output encoding before writing, and caller ownership/current position are preserved. Unsupported flags/content fail explicitly; native engine encoding defaults and WinRT ABI are not inferred. Portable byte decoding supports 874, 932, 936, 949, 950, 1250..1258, 10000, 10007 and 65001 through pinned encoding_rs tables. Raw/escaped multibyte tokens share one incremental UTF-16 decoder; malformed input and incomplete sequences at syntax boundaries fail without replacement. Font-scoped fcharset/cpg, default-font/plain resets, font names and field destinations share that codec. Symbol/OEM/Johab and unspecified pages remain explicit errors. Export retains the canonical Unicode-escaped writer; byte-for-byte native code-page roundtrip and full RTF content are not claimed. Paragraph/character stylesheet references now resolve forward based-on chains, additive formatting and subsequent direct overrides through the shared property decoder, with cycle/kind/reference/depth checks and an independent expansion work budget. Ignored style names/keycodes/metadata never become story text. Resolved appearance is retained; live named-style identity, next-style policies and section/table styles are not implemented. Hyperlink field results spanning paragraphs become separate paragraph-owned links with identical URI/target and retained metrics/formatting; empty paragraphs create no invisible links. Cumulative materialized URI/target bytes are checked against max_bytes before cloning. Imports finish parsing before model/history/preview mutation. Native field identity and full content/format conformance remain pending.

#### `M:Microsoft.UI.Text.RichEditTextDocument.SaveToStream(Microsoft.UI.Text.TextGetOptions,Windows.Storage.Streams.IRandomAccessStream)`

State: **partial**. The native random-access stream ABI is translated to FerroUI-style Rust Read/Write. TextStreamOptions explicitly selects plain UTF-8/UTF-16LE/UTF-16BE, BOM and byte bounds; RTF uses raw codec bytes. Input validation finishes before mutation, output encoding before writing, and caller ownership/current position are preserved. Unsupported flags/content fail explicitly; native engine encoding defaults and WinRT ABI are not inferred. The RTF writer retains Unicode-escaped canonical output; multilingual import/export fixtures validate text recovery without claiming preservation of original byte encoding or native full-content parity.

#### `M:Microsoft.UI.Text.RichEditTextDocument.SetText(Microsoft.UI.Text.TextSetOptions,System.String)`

State: **partial**. Typed get_text/set_text_with_options implement the mapped plain/RTF projections, CR/CRLF/LF and terminal-paragraph handling, scalar-safe length policy, atomic parse/option validation and supported Unlink insertion. The native UseLfAndUseCrLf assertions are adapted directly. Object-text, numbering, hidden-text filtering/unhiding, UnicodeBidi insertion mode and ApplyRtfDocumentDefaults return explicit UnsupportedOptions; unknown/contradictory flags fail before editing. The model retains normalized UTF-16 text coordinates and the codec remains a bounded RTF subset. Portable byte decoding supports 874, 932, 936, 949, 950, 1250..1258, 10000, 10007 and 65001 through pinned encoding_rs tables. Raw/escaped multibyte tokens share one incremental UTF-16 decoder; malformed input and incomplete sequences at syntax boundaries fail without replacement. Font-scoped fcharset/cpg, default-font/plain resets, font names and field destinations share that codec. Symbol/OEM/Johab and unspecified pages remain explicit errors. Export retains the canonical Unicode-escaped writer; byte-for-byte native code-page roundtrip and full RTF content are not claimed. Paragraph/character stylesheet references now resolve forward based-on chains, additive formatting and subsequent direct overrides through the shared property decoder, with cycle/kind/reference/depth checks and an independent expansion work budget. Ignored style names/keycodes/metadata never become story text. Resolved appearance is retained; live named-style identity, next-style policies and section/table styles are not implemented. Hyperlink field results spanning paragraphs become separate paragraph-owned links with identical URI/target and retained metrics/formatting; empty paragraphs create no invisible links. Cumulative materialized URI/target bytes are checked against max_bytes before cloning. Imports finish parsing before model/history/preview mutation. Native field identity and full content/format conformance remain pending.

### `Microsoft.UI.Text.RichEditTextRange`

Audit the external TOM contract member by member. The Rust facade uses typed errors, UTF-16 text ranges and shared editor services; remaining option behavior, ABI and native units are not inferred from similarly named methods. Eight native-valued units including shaped Cluster, explicit Rust Read/Write adapters, paragraph tabs and structured Unicode case conversion have individual mappings; locale/engine conformance and unmapped members remain pending.

#### `M:Microsoft.UI.Text.RichEditTextRange.CanPaste(System.Int32)`

State: **partial**. The TOM clipboard family uses injected FerroUI IClipboard and LocalBoxFuture services. BestAvailable chooses exact in-process content, then supported RTF aliases, then Unicode text; explicit PlainText/Rtf never fall back outside the requested representation. CanPaste checks fallible advertised formats without decoding payloads, ending composition or modifying history. Document CanCopy is permission, independent of selection length and edit read-only state; the current model has no copy-protection policy. Copy captures immutable visible content. Nonempty Cut ends an original preview before capturing committed content, then deletes only after a successful write and current-target validation; a failed write does not restart that preview. Paste validates/parses/limits before canceling an original preview and recaptures committed live endpoints. Empty or rejected content cannot delete the target. Plain text inherits insertion formatting; rich fragments retain supported structure; directed editor selection is rebased and the edit forms one undo group. Document mutation identity, shared range/format generation and a disposable editor-change subscription reject stale asynchronous edits, including away-and-back changes and held batches. Retrieved transfers dispose on success, error or future cancellation and before final validation; outgoing transfers belong to the clipboard. These asynchronous named-format APIs are an intentional Rust translation, not synchronous native ABI or arbitrary numeric-format support. Native copy/per-range protection, OLE cloning, unsupported formats/RTF grammar, terminal EOP and external WinUI behavior remain pending. Control routed clipboard events/casing policy is separate from this independent TOM range service. Test definitions and completed execution evidence are recorded separately.

#### `M:Microsoft.UI.Text.RichEditTextRange.ChangeCase(Microsoft.UI.Text.LetterCase)`

State: **partial**. Unicode default upper/lower casing preserves nested formatting, hyperlinks, embedded-control identity and paragraph boundaries. Whole-range contextual lowercase handles final sigma across run boundaries; scalar expansions remap independent directed selection and one grouped undo unit. No-op edits preserve revision/redo/composition, read-only/length failures reject mutation, and a changed operation recaptures committed content after preedit cancellation. Rust Unicode-version/locale behavior, native structural offsets and native engine conformance remain explicit boundaries.

#### `M:Microsoft.UI.Text.RichEditTextRange.Cut`

State: **partial**. The TOM clipboard family uses injected FerroUI IClipboard and LocalBoxFuture services. BestAvailable chooses exact in-process content, then supported RTF aliases, then Unicode text; explicit PlainText/Rtf never fall back outside the requested representation. CanPaste checks fallible advertised formats without decoding payloads, ending composition or modifying history. Document CanCopy is permission, independent of selection length and edit read-only state; the current model has no copy-protection policy. Copy captures immutable visible content. Nonempty Cut ends an original preview before capturing committed content, then deletes only after a successful write and current-target validation; a failed write does not restart that preview. Paste validates/parses/limits before canceling an original preview and recaptures committed live endpoints. Empty or rejected content cannot delete the target. Plain text inherits insertion formatting; rich fragments retain supported structure; directed editor selection is rebased and the edit forms one undo group. Document mutation identity, shared range/format generation and a disposable editor-change subscription reject stale asynchronous edits, including away-and-back changes and held batches. Retrieved transfers dispose on success, error or future cancellation and before final validation; outgoing transfers belong to the clipboard. These asynchronous named-format APIs are an intentional Rust translation, not synchronous native ABI or arbitrary numeric-format support. Native copy/per-range protection, OLE cloning, unsupported formats/RTF grammar, terminal EOP and external WinUI behavior remain pending. Control routed clipboard events/casing policy is separate from this independent TOM range service. Test definitions and completed execution evidence are recorded separately.

#### `M:Microsoft.UI.Text.RichEditTextRange.Delete(Microsoft.UI.Text.TextRangeUnit,System.Int32)`

State: **partial**. Delete removes a nonempty range first and counts it once, then resolves remaining signed logical units against the changed document. Count zero removes only the selected span; extreme counts do not overflow. Supported paragraph joins retain the surviving following paragraph format, preserve local/inherited character provenance, rebase independent selection and collapse the edited range in one undo unit. The selection facade recaptures after layout callbacks. Proven external model changes during layout or publication survive rejection without stale history/selection rollback; ordinary errors still roll back. The Rust result is a nonnegative usize removed-unit count. Only the eight mapped units and normalized model positions are supported; native structural markers, additional units and native engine conformance remain pending.

#### `M:Microsoft.UI.Text.RichEditTextRange.EndOf(Microsoft.UI.Text.TextRangeUnit,System.Boolean)`

State: **partial**. end_of operates on live scalar-safe UTF-16 ranges. Start/end use signed displacements, indices are one-based or end-relative, and movement counts a nonempty collapse as its first unit. The eight implemented constants retain native numeric values. Character traverses Unicode scalars, Word includes following ASCII blanks, Sentence follows native punctuation rules, Paragraph handles native separators, HardParagraph distinguishes structural paragraphs from soft breaks, and Line uses a weak complete untrimmed view with headless Paragraph fallback. The model has one Story and excludes the synthetic terminal CR. Remaining native units, arbitrary stories and ABI remain pending. Shaped Cluster uses the same movement/index operations and requires complete validated live layout.

#### `M:Microsoft.UI.Text.RichEditTextRange.Paste(System.Int32)`

State: **partial**. The TOM clipboard family uses injected FerroUI IClipboard and LocalBoxFuture services. BestAvailable chooses exact in-process content, then supported RTF aliases, then Unicode text; explicit PlainText/Rtf never fall back outside the requested representation. CanPaste checks fallible advertised formats without decoding payloads, ending composition or modifying history. Document CanCopy is permission, independent of selection length and edit read-only state; the current model has no copy-protection policy. Copy captures immutable visible content. Nonempty Cut ends an original preview before capturing committed content, then deletes only after a successful write and current-target validation; a failed write does not restart that preview. Paste validates/parses/limits before canceling an original preview and recaptures committed live endpoints. Empty or rejected content cannot delete the target. Plain text inherits insertion formatting; rich fragments retain supported structure; directed editor selection is rebased and the edit forms one undo group. Document mutation identity, shared range/format generation and a disposable editor-change subscription reject stale asynchronous edits, including away-and-back changes and held batches. Retrieved transfers dispose on success, error or future cancellation and before final validation; outgoing transfers belong to the clipboard. These asynchronous named-format APIs are an intentional Rust translation, not synchronous native ABI or arbitrary numeric-format support. Native copy/per-range protection, OLE cloning, unsupported formats/RTF grammar, terminal EOP and external WinUI behavior remain pending. Control routed clipboard events/casing policy is separate from this independent TOM range service. Test definitions and completed execution evidence are recorded separately.

#### `M:Microsoft.UI.Text.RichEditTextRange.SetIndex(Microsoft.UI.Text.TextRangeUnit,System.Int32,System.Boolean)`

State: **partial**. set_index operates on live scalar-safe UTF-16 ranges. Start/end use signed displacements, indices are one-based or end-relative, and movement counts a nonempty collapse as its first unit. The eight implemented constants retain native numeric values. Character traverses Unicode scalars, Word includes following ASCII blanks, Sentence follows native punctuation rules, Paragraph handles native separators, HardParagraph distinguishes structural paragraphs from soft breaks, and Line uses a weak complete untrimmed view with headless Paragraph fallback. The model has one Story and excludes the synthetic terminal CR. Remaining native units, arbitrary stories and ABI remain pending. Shaped Cluster uses the same movement/index operations and requires complete validated live layout.

#### `M:Microsoft.UI.Text.RichEditTextRange.SetText(Microsoft.UI.Text.TextSetOptions,System.String)`

State: **partial**. The range operation uses shared live text positions and typed Result values. Unit movement and search use the documented Rust subset; native options, count conventions and geometry flags remain adapted. Portable byte decoding supports 874, 932, 936, 949, 950, 1250..1258, 10000, 10007 and 65001 through pinned encoding_rs tables. Raw/escaped multibyte tokens share one incremental UTF-16 decoder; malformed input and incomplete sequences at syntax boundaries fail without replacement. Font-scoped fcharset/cpg, default-font/plain resets, font names and field destinations share that codec. Symbol/OEM/Johab and unspecified pages remain explicit errors. Export retains the canonical Unicode-escaped writer; byte-for-byte native code-page roundtrip and full RTF content are not claimed. Paragraph/character stylesheet references now resolve forward based-on chains, additive formatting and subsequent direct overrides through the shared property decoder, with cycle/kind/reference/depth checks and an independent expansion work budget. Ignored style names/keycodes/metadata never become story text. Resolved appearance is retained; live named-style identity, next-style policies and section/table styles are not implemented. Hyperlink field results spanning paragraphs become separate paragraph-owned links with identical URI/target and retained metrics/formatting; empty paragraphs create no invisible links. Cumulative materialized URI/target bytes are checked against max_bytes before cloning. Imports finish parsing before model/history/preview mutation. Native field identity and full content/format conformance remain pending.

#### `M:Microsoft.UI.Text.RichEditTextRange.SetTextViaStream(Microsoft.UI.Text.TextSetOptions,Windows.Storage.Streams.IRandomAccessStream)`

State: **partial**. The native random-access stream ABI is translated to FerroUI-style Rust Read/Write. TextStreamOptions explicitly selects plain UTF-8/UTF-16LE/UTF-16BE, BOM and byte bounds; RTF uses raw codec bytes. Input validation finishes before mutation, output encoding before writing, and caller ownership/current position are preserved. Unsupported flags/content fail explicitly; native engine encoding defaults and WinRT ABI are not inferred. Portable byte decoding supports 874, 932, 936, 949, 950, 1250..1258, 10000, 10007 and 65001 through pinned encoding_rs tables. Raw/escaped multibyte tokens share one incremental UTF-16 decoder; malformed input and incomplete sequences at syntax boundaries fail without replacement. Font-scoped fcharset/cpg, default-font/plain resets, font names and field destinations share that codec. Symbol/OEM/Johab and unspecified pages remain explicit errors. Export retains the canonical Unicode-escaped writer; byte-for-byte native code-page roundtrip and full RTF content are not claimed. Paragraph/character stylesheet references now resolve forward based-on chains, additive formatting and subsequent direct overrides through the shared property decoder, with cycle/kind/reference/depth checks and an independent expansion work budget. Ignored style names/keycodes/metadata never become story text. Resolved appearance is retained; live named-style identity, next-style policies and section/table styles are not implemented. Hyperlink field results spanning paragraphs become separate paragraph-owned links with identical URI/target and retained metrics/formatting; empty paragraphs create no invisible links. Cumulative materialized URI/target bytes are checked against max_bytes before cloning. Imports finish parsing before model/history/preview mutation. Native field identity and full content/format conformance remain pending.

#### `M:Microsoft.UI.Text.RichEditTextRange.StartOf(Microsoft.UI.Text.TextRangeUnit,System.Boolean)`

State: **partial**. start_of operates on live scalar-safe UTF-16 ranges. Start/end use signed displacements, indices are one-based or end-relative, and movement counts a nonempty collapse as its first unit. The eight implemented constants retain native numeric values. Character traverses Unicode scalars, Word includes following ASCII blanks, Sentence follows native punctuation rules, Paragraph handles native separators, HardParagraph distinguishes structural paragraphs from soft breaks, and Line uses a weak complete untrimmed view with headless Paragraph fallback. The model has one Story and excludes the synthetic terminal CR. Remaining native units, arbitrary stories and ABI remain pending. Shaped Cluster uses the same movement/index operations and requires complete validated live layout.

#### `P:Microsoft.UI.Text.RichEditTextRange.Character`

State: **partial**. Character reads the exact UTF-16 code unit at the range start, including a leading surrogate, and returns zero at the model end. The u16 setter rejects isolated surrogate input and replacement of half an existing pair; Rust scalar getter/setter extensions handle complete supplementary characters safely. Replacement retains assigned run/container/paragraph formatting and inheritance, the range start, independent directed selection, scalar-safe length policy and one undo unit. Preflight validation/no-op calls preserve composition and redo; changed calls cancel preview then recapture committed content, which can itself be unchanged. Detected external writes retain their model while stale history/composition is discarded. Native synthetic terminal CR and transient malformed UTF-16 are not model characters; native engine conformance remains pending.

#### `P:Microsoft.UI.Text.RichEditTextRange.Gravity`

State: **partial**. Independent ranges retain native-valued formatting affinity, including measured Outward-to-UI readback and duplicate reset-to-UI. Collapsed format queries and plain SetText/paste use the same previous/following-run resolution; explicit patches override the resolved source, and paragraph formatting stays with the current paragraph. Native 45 affinity, ten retention and 24 invalid fixtures are literal tests. Range generations preserve newer callback ownership and invalidate pending clipboard work; grouped edits restore the exact independent typing snapshot. Native physical endpoint rebasing differs from current TextPointer tracking and is not changed here. The model excludes a synthetic terminal EOP, so forward story-end affinity samples final paragraph defaults; signed native clamping is adapted to scalar-safe usize/Result validation. The actual selection's inherited Gravity behavior and the external WinUI engine remain unmeasured. Range metadata is not document history; successful undo and failed outer text groups retain accepted explicit mode changes as a stated FerroUI policy.

#### `T:Microsoft.UI.Text.TextRangeUnit`

State: **partial**. The eight implemented constants retain native numeric values. Character traverses Unicode scalars, Word includes following ASCII blanks, Sentence follows native punctuation rules, Paragraph handles native separators, HardParagraph distinguishes structural paragraphs from soft breaks, and Line uses a weak complete untrimmed view with headless Paragraph fallback. The model has one Story and excludes the synthetic terminal CR. Remaining native units, arbitrary stories and ABI remain pending. Cluster retains native value 13 and derives logical UTF-16 unit boundaries from the associated formatter shaping output, including ligatures, script clusters, omitted break glyphs, inline controls, soft breaks and linked pages. It requires complete untrimmed live layout, has no grapheme fallback, and rejects stale or malformed layout boundaries. Exact native shaper and platform behavior remain separate conformance work.

#### `F:Microsoft.UI.Text.TextSetOptions.FormatRtf`

State: **partial**. Native numeric flags and FerroUI markup metadata are declared by the Rust type. Only the associated mapped operations implement flag behavior; unsupported modes return typed errors before mutation. This record does not count declaration of an unsupported flag as functional implementation of that mode. Portable byte decoding supports 874, 932, 936, 949, 950, 1250..1258, 10000, 10007 and 65001 through pinned encoding_rs tables. Raw/escaped multibyte tokens share one incremental UTF-16 decoder; malformed input and incomplete sequences at syntax boundaries fail without replacement. Font-scoped fcharset/cpg, default-font/plain resets, font names and field destinations share that codec. Symbol/OEM/Johab and unspecified pages remain explicit errors. Export retains the canonical Unicode-escaped writer; byte-for-byte native code-page roundtrip and full RTF content are not claimed. Paragraph/character stylesheet references now resolve forward based-on chains, additive formatting and subsequent direct overrides through the shared property decoder, with cycle/kind/reference/depth checks and an independent expansion work budget. Ignored style names/keycodes/metadata never become story text. Resolved appearance is retained; live named-style identity, next-style policies and section/table styles are not implemented. Hyperlink field results spanning paragraphs become separate paragraph-owned links with identical URI/target and retained metrics/formatting; empty paragraphs create no invisible links. Cumulative materialized URI/target bytes are checked against max_bytes before cloning. Imports finish parsing before model/history/preview mutation. Native field identity and full content/format conformance remain pending.

### `Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Automation.Provider.ITextEditProvider`

Review text provider/range/peer members individually, including attributes, units, platform marshalling, weak lifetime, events and native clients. Text2 caret, TextChild, accepted-composition TextEdit and public peer/EventsSource events have mapped implementations; conversion-target backend data, annotations, unsupported attributes and native client conformance remain explicit pending contracts.

#### `M:Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Automation.Provider.ITextEditProvider.GetActiveComposition`

State: **partial**. TextEdit inherits Text independently of Text2. The editor returns the full active accepted IME preview as a live weak UTF-16 range, or None without an active composition; retained ranges follow owner/document lifetime. Accepted preview delta and single finalization events rewire on model replacement and marshal through the Win32 UI-thread bridge. A distinct conversion target requires backend data and is currently absent. Public AutomationPeer.RaiseTextEditTextChangedEvent and weak EventsSource routing are implemented; system cause producers and native Windows client execution remain pending.

### `Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.ContextMenuEventArgs`

Review editable control members, native event timing, IME/clipboard capabilities, templates, accelerators and automation. Missing members are omitted, not stubbed.

#### `P:Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.ContextMenuEventArgs.CursorLeft`

State: **partial**. RichEditBox now projects pointer, Apps/Shift+F10 and holding ContextRequested into one synchronous bubble ContextMenuOpening before default menu dispatch. Immutable f64 CursorLeft/Top use root DIPs and shared inherited Handled cancels the request. Keyboard anchors use the normalized LTR end/bottom or RTL start/bottom selected grapheme edge, independently of directed anchor, with shaped caret fallback and soft-wrap retention. The edge is selected in presenter coordinates before transforming the point, preserving the selected side under reflection/rotation. Weak per-request rectangles carry the actual anchor through existing ContextMenu/PopupFlyoutBase lifecycle, RTL gravity and constrained popup positioning; zero-size points remain valid. Handlers may install/replace/remove menus; nested requests, stale layout and detach/reattach are fenced, canceled openings are consumed once, and existing precedence/focus/IME retention remain shared. Ordinary popup dismissal retains composition and the semantic connection by avoiding a redundant unchanged-view requery during GotFocus; a real redirected focus retires that session. Routed metadata and named runtime/compiled handlers use the live base-argument handle. Native automatic selection floaties, legacy asynchronous command-gated PopupMenu, exact native edge metrics and close/reopen event order remain pending. An already open owned FerroUI popup is repositioned in place; this does not claim native WinUI flyout or platform event conformance. Test definitions and their actual completed execution records are tracked separately. The keyboard records its accepted destination in the shared input manager before LostFocus/GotFocus, while ordinary client installation remains after those events. Legitimate synchronous template/view requery now resolves the accepted owner and preserves an owned-popup composition. Accepted focus generations fence nested Losing/Getting/Lost/Got transitions, including round trips; canceled nested requests do not supersede an outer accepted transition. Input-client and view-accessor callbacks recheck both binding and focus identity. This covers synchronous framework focus/requery ownership, not arbitrary native asynchronous focus order.

State: **partial**. Routed framework notification/cancellation is connected to the rich editor operation. Native argument shape, exact timing and the complete event sequence remain explicitly adapted. Exact native input requests retain the UTF-16 replacement range, replacement text and resulting directed selection through the shared connection and rich editor. Empty replacements delete their requested range. Composition retains its whole active span independently of the caret, commits once and keeps the original cancellation snapshot. Invalid or filtered/limited/cancelled/reentrant requests reject success. CoreText keeps last-acknowledged state separate from current state so failed notifications retry from the old native length and late/reentrant acknowledgements cannot hide newer state. Unsupported CoreText clause formatting reports Failed; legacy TextBox transport and actual OS conformance remain separate. The three native composition argument classes map to one routed Rust RichEditCompositionEventArgs with readonly signed StartIndex/Length, native unavailable defaults -1/0, accepted replacement text and directed selection. Ranges count normalized UTF-16 model positions and cover the whole accepted composition independently of its caret. Cursor-only movement emits no changed event; filtered/truncated commit payloads report accepted text. Reentrant changes before end publication suppress stale successful completion reporting. Changes made by an Ended handler invalidate the native acknowledgement after event delivery. Shared Rust argument identity, FerroUI model coordinates, native nested asynchronous event dispatch and real backend ordering remain explicit differences. Explicit native begin captures committed content/selection without mutation or history, immediately raises empty 0/0 started args, and keeps active_composition_range absent until an accepted update. First exact replacement establishes its own extent. Empty completion/cancel closes once without undo or lost redo; legacy first-preedit implicit startup remains supported. Reentrant end/start callbacks cannot replace a newer session with an older request. Pending automation range absence is a framework projection; native pre-update automation and nested asynchronous event dispatch remain conformance boundaries.

#### `E:Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.RichEditBox.TextCompositionStarted`

State: **partial**. Routed framework notification/cancellation is connected to the rich editor operation. Native argument shape, exact timing and the complete event sequence remain explicitly adapted. Exact native input requests retain the UTF-16 replacement range, replacement text and resulting directed selection through the shared connection and rich editor. Empty replacements delete their requested range. Composition retains its whole active span independently of the caret, commits once and keeps the original cancellation snapshot. Invalid or filtered/limited/cancelled/reentrant requests reject success. CoreText keeps last-acknowledged state separate from current state so failed notifications retry from the old native length and late/reentrant acknowledgements cannot hide newer state. Unsupported CoreText clause formatting reports Failed; legacy TextBox transport and actual OS conformance remain separate. The three native composition argument classes map to one routed Rust RichEditCompositionEventArgs with readonly signed StartIndex/Length, native unavailable defaults -1/0, accepted replacement text and directed selection. Ranges count normalized UTF-16 model positions and cover the whole accepted composition independently of its caret. Cursor-only movement emits no changed event; filtered/truncated commit payloads report accepted text. Reentrant changes before end publication suppress stale successful completion reporting. Changes made by an Ended handler invalidate the native acknowledgement after event delivery. Shared Rust argument identity, FerroUI model coordinates, native nested asynchronous event dispatch and real backend ordering remain explicit differences. Explicit native begin captures committed content/selection without mutation or history, immediately raises empty 0/0 started args, and keeps active_composition_range absent until an accepted update. First exact replacement establishes its own extent. Empty completion/cancel closes once without undo or lost redo; legacy first-preedit implicit startup remains supported. Reentrant end/start callbacks cannot replace a newer session with an older request. Pending automation range absence is a framework projection; native pre-update automation and nested asynchronous event dispatch remain conformance boundaries.

#### `P:Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.RichEditBox.DescriptionProperty`

State: **partial**. RichEditBox is a FerroUI TemplatedControl with one persistent RichEditBoxTextPresenter and shared model/editor/history. ContentElement accepts framework content hosts; header, placeholder and description use actual optional parts. Internal logical scrolling measures the full document at viewport width, keeps chrome fixed and shares text/caret/IME/automation offsets. Retemplating preserves live services, composition and undo. Owner-routed focus/selection and raw presenter automation avoid duplicate identity. Native windowless ABI, full backend services, touch UI and unmapped members remain pending.

#### `P:Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.RichEditBox.HeaderTemplate`

State: **partial**. RichEditBox is a FerroUI TemplatedControl with one persistent RichEditBoxTextPresenter and shared model/editor/history. ContentElement accepts framework content hosts; header, placeholder and description use actual optional parts. Internal logical scrolling measures the full document at viewport width, keeps chrome fixed and shares text/caret/IME/automation offsets. Retemplating preserves live services, composition and undo. Owner-routed focus/selection and raw presenter automation avoid duplicate identity. Native windowless ABI, full backend services, touch UI and unmapped members remain pending.

#### `P:Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.RichEditBox.InputScope`

State: **partial**. RichEditBox.InputScope is a nullable styled Option<Ref<InputScope>> with weak subscriptions to replacement, ordered Names mutations and shared NameValue changes. It publishes immutable complete snapshots through inherited TextInputOptions without overwriting legacy hints, client identity, composition or history; clear/empty restores the independent fallback. Semantic ownership persists through owned flyouts, and generation fences make newer policy win during callbacks. CoreText preserves exact names and lazy/reentrant/retry delivery; Android, iOS, Wayland, Fcitx and IBus project supported purpose/keyboard hints. Single-purpose consumers select the first name; IMM32 forwards every name with native equal weighting and independent IS_PRIVATE, associates the same-thread HWND, retries failures and clears retired identities. Optional AppKit delivery preserves the existing native ABI and provides four supported macOS 14 content meanings, clearing unsupported/private/disabled hints. Browser uses one persistent LF-projected textarea with exact UTF-16 transactions; CR/CRLF model text remains exact and unrepresentable boundaries reject safely. Suggestions are enabled only for exact-edit nonprivate clients. Actual OS/device keyboard, prediction, candidate-window, proofing and WinRT collection/activation behavior remain separate. IMM32 does not provide a TSF Document Manager or guarantee touch-keyboard notifications; AppKit exact replacement/proofing remains pending. Source mappings and completed execution records are independent.

#### `P:Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.RichEditBox.InputScopeProperty`

State: **partial**. The registered nullable FerroUI styled InputScope property stores shared InputScope objects and drives weak scope/list/item subscriptions and immutable input-option snapshots. Runtime and compiled markup accept the native named shortcut, explicit Names objects and x:Null. Clearing restores existing independently configured content hints. FerroUI property metadata/ownership replace the dependency-property ABI; actual OS keyboard policy and complete native property semantics remain partial under RT-I20.

#### `P:Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.RichEditBox.IsTextPredictionEnabled`

State: **partial**. The rich control registers and consumes this input/presentation value through FerroUI. Backend capabilities, complete native presentation and every platform edge case remain separate. Effective changes to all ten attached TextInputOptions are observed on the semantic owner, including inherited/cleared values, without resetting composition or replacing the client/connection. Weak subscriptions survive reset and are disposed on owner replacement/teardown. Reentrant same-transport setter completion reapplies the newest owner policies; initial client installation retains its generation fence. The immutable ordered InputScope.Names snapshot now accompanies existing option transport; native prediction/proofing and multi-name negotiation remain separate.

#### `T:Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.RichEditBox`

State: **partial**. RichEditBox derives from FerroUI TemplatedControl and owns one persistent RichEditBoxTextPresenter with shared model, layout, directed selection, history and input services. Real template parts and retemplating retain composition and live services. Native windowless ABI, remaining platform services and unmapped public members remain pending. RichEditBox now projects pointer, Apps/Shift+F10 and holding ContextRequested into one synchronous bubble ContextMenuOpening before default menu dispatch. Immutable f64 CursorLeft/Top use root DIPs and shared inherited Handled cancels the request. Keyboard anchors use the normalized LTR end/bottom or RTL start/bottom selected grapheme edge, independently of directed anchor, with shaped caret fallback and soft-wrap retention. The edge is selected in presenter coordinates before transforming the point, preserving the selected side under reflection/rotation. Weak per-request rectangles carry the actual anchor through existing ContextMenu/PopupFlyoutBase lifecycle, RTL gravity and constrained popup positioning; zero-size points remain valid. Handlers may install/replace/remove menus; nested requests, stale layout and detach/reattach are fenced, canceled openings are consumed once, and existing precedence/focus/IME retention remain shared. Ordinary popup dismissal retains composition and the semantic connection by avoiding a redundant unchanged-view requery during GotFocus; a real redirected focus retires that session. Routed metadata and named runtime/compiled handlers use the live base-argument handle. Native automatic selection floaties, legacy asynchronous command-gated PopupMenu, exact native edge metrics and close/reopen event order remain pending. An already open owned FerroUI popup is repositioned in place; this does not claim native WinUI flyout or platform event conformance. Test definitions and their actual completed execution records are tracked separately. The keyboard records its accepted destination in the shared input manager before LostFocus/GotFocus, while ordinary client installation remains after those events. Legitimate synchronous template/view requery now resolves the accepted owner and preserves an owned-popup composition. Accepted focus generations fence nested Losing/Getting/Lost/Got transitions, including round trips; canceled nested requests do not supersede an outer accepted transition. Input-client and view-accessor callbacks recheck both binding and focus identity. This covers synchronous framework focus/requery ownership, not arbitrary native asynchronous focus order.

### `Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.RichEditBoxSelectionChangingEventArgs`

Review editable control members, native event timing, IME/clipboard capabilities, templates, accelerators and automation. Missing members are omitted, not stubbed.

#### `P:Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.RichEditBoxSelectionChangingEventArgs.Cancel`

State: **partial**. SelectionChanging exposes the proposed view/TOM selection and a shared Cancel flag before publication. Cancellation preserves the prior selection, while reentrant view or TOM selection overrides cancellation and publishes the final selection once. Temporary grouped edit ranges stay internal; accepted post-edit selection participates in undo/redo. Native ABI and backend input scenarios remain separate acceptance work. Markup metadata receives the framework shared Rc<dyn IRoutedEventArgs> handle, downcasts checked payload access, and inherits the routed base. Runtime and generated code-behind can accept RoutedEventArgs while typed Rust subscribers observe the same live payload/Cancel/Handled state; concrete-value metadata previously rejected that actual handler representation.

Review editable control members, native event timing, IME/clipboard capabilities, templates, accelerators and automation. Missing members are omitted, not stubbed.

#### `P:Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.TextCompositionChangedEventArgs.Length`

State: **partial**. The three native composition argument classes map to one routed Rust RichEditCompositionEventArgs with readonly signed StartIndex/Length, native unavailable defaults -1/0, accepted replacement text and directed selection. Ranges count normalized UTF-16 model positions and cover the whole accepted composition independently of its caret. Cursor-only movement emits no changed event; filtered/truncated commit payloads report accepted text. Reentrant changes before end publication suppress stale successful completion reporting. Changes made by an Ended handler invalidate the native acknowledgement after event delivery. Shared Rust argument identity, FerroUI model coordinates, native nested asynchronous event dispatch and real backend ordering remain explicit differences. Explicit native begin captures committed content/selection without mutation or history, immediately raises empty 0/0 started args, and keeps active_composition_range absent until an accepted update. First exact replacement establishes its own extent. Empty completion/cancel closes once without undo or lost redo; legacy first-preedit implicit startup remains supported. Reentrant end/start callbacks cannot replace a newer session with an older request. Pending automation range absence is a framework projection; native pre-update automation and nested asynchronous event dispatch remain conformance boundaries. Markup metadata receives the framework shared Rc<dyn IRoutedEventArgs> handle, downcasts checked payload access, and inherits the routed base. Runtime and generated code-behind can accept RoutedEventArgs while typed Rust subscribers observe the same live payload/Cancel/Handled state; concrete-value metadata previously rejected that actual handler representation.

#### `P:Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.TextCompositionChangedEventArgs.StartIndex`

State: **partial**. The three native composition argument classes map to one routed Rust RichEditCompositionEventArgs with readonly signed StartIndex/Length, native unavailable defaults -1/0, accepted replacement text and directed selection. Ranges count normalized UTF-16 model positions and cover the whole accepted composition independently of its caret. Cursor-only movement emits no changed event; filtered/truncated commit payloads report accepted text. Reentrant changes before end publication suppress stale successful completion reporting. Changes made by an Ended handler invalidate the native acknowledgement after event delivery. Shared Rust argument identity, FerroUI model coordinates, native nested asynchronous event dispatch and real backend ordering remain explicit differences. Explicit native begin captures committed content/selection without mutation or history, immediately raises empty 0/0 started args, and keeps active_composition_range absent until an accepted update. First exact replacement establishes its own extent. Empty completion/cancel closes once without undo or lost redo; legacy first-preedit implicit startup remains supported. Reentrant end/start callbacks cannot replace a newer session with an older request. Pending automation range absence is a framework projection; native pre-update automation and nested asynchronous event dispatch remain conformance boundaries. Markup metadata receives the framework shared Rc<dyn IRoutedEventArgs> handle, downcasts checked payload access, and inherits the routed base. Runtime and generated code-behind can accept RoutedEventArgs while typed Rust subscribers observe the same live payload/Cancel/Handled state; concrete-value metadata previously rejected that actual handler representation.

#### `T:Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.TextCompositionEndedEventArgs`

State: **partial**. The three native composition argument classes map to one routed Rust RichEditCompositionEventArgs with readonly signed StartIndex/Length, native unavailable defaults -1/0, accepted replacement text and directed selection. Ranges count normalized UTF-16 model positions and cover the whole accepted composition independently of its caret. Cursor-only movement emits no changed event; filtered/truncated commit payloads report accepted text. Reentrant changes before end publication suppress stale successful completion reporting. Changes made by an Ended handler invalidate the native acknowledgement after event delivery. Shared Rust argument identity, FerroUI model coordinates, native nested asynchronous event dispatch and real backend ordering remain explicit differences. Explicit native begin captures committed content/selection without mutation or history, immediately raises empty 0/0 started args, and keeps active_composition_range absent until an accepted update. First exact replacement establishes its own extent. Empty completion/cancel closes once without undo or lost redo; legacy first-preedit implicit startup remains supported. Reentrant end/start callbacks cannot replace a newer session with an older request. Pending automation range absence is a framework projection; native pre-update automation and nested asynchronous event dispatch remain conformance boundaries. Markup metadata receives the framework shared Rc<dyn IRoutedEventArgs> handle, downcasts checked payload access, and inherits the routed base. Runtime and generated code-behind can accept RoutedEventArgs while typed Rust subscribers observe the same live payload/Cancel/Handled state; concrete-value metadata previously rejected that actual handler representation.

#### `T:Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.TextCompositionStartedEventArgs`

State: **partial**. The three native composition argument classes map to one routed Rust RichEditCompositionEventArgs with readonly signed StartIndex/Length, native unavailable defaults -1/0, accepted replacement text and directed selection. Ranges count normalized UTF-16 model positions and cover the whole accepted composition independently of its caret. Cursor-only movement emits no changed event; filtered/truncated commit payloads report accepted text. Reentrant changes before end publication suppress stale successful completion reporting. Changes made by an Ended handler invalidate the native acknowledgement after event delivery. Shared Rust argument identity, FerroUI model coordinates, native nested asynchronous event dispatch and real backend ordering remain explicit differences. Explicit native begin captures committed content/selection without mutation or history, immediately raises empty 0/0 started args, and keeps active_composition_range absent until an accepted update. First exact replacement establishes its own extent. Empty completion/cancel closes once without undo or lost redo; legacy first-preedit implicit startup remains supported. Reentrant end/start callbacks cannot replace a newer session with an older request. Pending automation range absence is a framework projection; native pre-update automation and nested asynchronous event dispatch remain conformance boundaries. Markup metadata receives the framework shared Rc<dyn IRoutedEventArgs> handle, downcasts checked payload access, and inherits the routed base. Runtime and generated code-behind can accept RoutedEventArgs while typed Rust subscribers observe the same live payload/Cancel/Handled state; concrete-value metadata previously rejected that actual handler representation.

### `Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Documents.TextElement`

Review each document property, collection identity, inherited formatting, invalidation, markup and observable edge case against the pinned source.

#### `M:Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Documents.TextElement.FindName(System.String)`

State: **partial**. TextElement delegates to the current nearest FerroUI NameScopeExtensions scope and its find implementation, returning the same live registered object as controls and other text elements. No scope/registration returns None, lookup rechecks reparenting/replaced scopes and holds no scope owner alive. Existing XAML x:Name and per-template-instance registration are exercised through runtime XAML. Equivalence is partial: FerroUI ChildNameScope falls back to its parent after completion, while ordinary nested NameScope is isolated; runtime Name/registration follows StyledElement and explicit NameScope policy. WinUI deferred element realization and automatic runtime renaming/registration are not provided. Template application attaches its actual result scope before callbacks while preserving explicit root scopes; a private weak parent adapter avoids retaining named owners and declaring trees. Real runtime-XAML template lookup, reapplication and destruction are covered without test-side scope attachment. Pending async completion after destruction of an incomplete parent retains existing framework policy. Deferred resources retain a weak scope-chain context so a nested template can skip an expired temporary construction scope and still resolve its live declaring scope, without retaining either named tree or bypassing a live incomplete scope.

#### `P:Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Documents.TextElement.Language`

State: **partial**. Inherited CultureInfo Language and CharacterFormat language patches use pinned XML-language validation, platform preferred language/en-US default, and existing culture-aware shaping/font fallback. Empty resolves to the application language. Windows ResolveLocaleName/MUI fallback and every LCID are not supplied by the finite portable culture table. RTF supports known deflang/lang and plain reset; unknown/unrepresentable language data fails explicitly.

All 43 named attached properties, 86 accessors, seven enum types and 38 values now map to inherited FerroUI properties and ordered OpenType features. Fresh tests cover inheritance, snapshots, mutable raw overrides, every text consumer, real HarfBuzz shaping and XAML. Keep native font/script raster conformance, exact native feature collection order and unsupported RTF typography outside completed claims; see TYPOGRAPHY.md and RT-I25.
